what_it_does: As AI data centers and supercomputers scale toward operating at truly enormous speeds (the next frontier beyond current 'exascale' systems), the network connecting thousands of chips together becomes a critical bottleneck — not just in raw bandwidth, but in how flexibly the network can be subdivided to give each running job its own isolated, fast communication channel without interference from neighbors. Existing network layouts ('topologies') like fat-tree (a hierarchy of switches resembling an upside-down tree) or dragonfly (groups of chips connected to a shared hub, with inter-group links) cannot efficiently carve out these isolated subnetworks for the small-to-medium job sizes that actually dominate real cluster usage. Zettafly is a new two-level network layout where the bottom layer consists of pre-defined self-contained groups of chips that communicate among themselves with no bottleneck (called 'non-blocking'), sized to match common job sizes, and the top layer connects these groups through a small number of shared routers. Any message between groups passes through at most one of these shared routers, keeping delays low while preserving the isolated fast zones inside each group.
